adopted_specification.heatmap: Single blue hue, Normalize(-400,1000), no clipping

comparison.grouping_and_order: The same 20 sender and 20 receiver labels and the aligned genome-status strips remain in the same visible order. No grouping or strain lookup change is observed.
comparison.pattern_visibility: The strongest top sender rows remain visibly darker than the remaining matrix. The baseline makes moderate differences more chromatically conspicuous; the candidate gives one ordered magnitude cue with no named hue transitions.
comparison.scientific_reading_task: Candidate preferred for the adopted absolute-minute reading task: one uninterrupted blue ramp with eight equally spaced 200-minute ticks, and both marginal axes explicitly showing the same 0–700 numeric range.
comparison.alignment: Receiver bars, sender bars and both binary strips remain aligned to matrix columns/rows. Genome tiles have visible outlined-white versus solid-charcoal states and matching guide keys.
comparison.guide_readability: The final colorbar title, all eight ticks, receiver-axis title and genome legend appear separate and readable in the complete panel. No visually apparent clipping, label collision or missing glyph is observed. The 57 × 3 mm colorbar remains subordinate to the 96 × 96 mm data region.
comparison.styling: Opaque bright-blue marginal bars remain borderless; binary states retain purposeful charcoal boundaries. Dark text and axes provide contrast against white space.
comparison.limits: Preference is scoped to this dataset and the adopted globally linear full-range task. It does not establish better sign decoding, finer discrimination among small 100–200 min differences, universal superiority, or publication acceptance.

findings.evidence: The darker first three sender rows and isolated stronger cells remain visible. Most of the remaining cells occupy a narrow part of the same blue ramp; the displayed IQR is 79.1904777225–200.663884225 min under the complete −400–1000 min range.
findings.requirement: Retain one globally linear full-source scale; make no claim of improved decoding of tiny effects.
findings.action: Accepted limitation. Retain the full range and avoid a claim of fine-effect discrimination or universal palette superiority.

findings.location: Zero and sign in the heatmap/colorbar
findings.evidence: Zero is a readable guide tick at 2/7 of the colorbar. The continuous single-hue ramp does not create a distinct white center or signed hue boundary.
findings.requirement: Honor the adopted single-hue global linear mapping while retaining the signed measurement definition.
findings.action: Accepted adaptation. The separate caption states the positive/negative meaning and the source GII > 300 min inhibition criterion; no new classification is drawn.

findings.evidence: Both visible numeric axes use 0, 350 and 700 min. The receiver value axis is 16 mm high and the sender value axis is 28 mm wide, corresponding to 2.2857142857 and 4 mm per 100 min.
findings.requirement: Share numeric 0–700 min limits without claiming identical physical bar-length scaling.
findings.action: Accepted limitation. Compare values through ticks; the caption explicitly distinguishes numeric limits from physical lengths.
